About The Role
We're looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist to join our team!
You'll focus on recruiting top talent across Engineering, Product, and Design, partnering directly with hiring managers and company leaders to help us scale.
This is a hands-on recruiting role. We're not looking for someone focused on HR, legal, or primarily sales hiring. We want someone who enjoys finding exceptional technical talent, building strong relationships, and thriving in a fast-moving startup where everyone jumps in to help.
We're looking for someone who has recruited in startup environments before and is comfortable wearing multiple hats, moving quickly, and figuring things out as they go.
What You'll Do
Own full-cycle recruiting for Engineering, Product, and Design roles.
Partner with hiring managers and founders to understand hiring needs and build recruiting strategies.
Source and engage outstanding passive candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, referrals, networking, and creative sourcing techniques.
Manage multiple searches while delivering excellent candidate experience.
Coordinate interviews, collect feedback, and help move candidates efficiently through the hiring process.
Build strong pipelines for current and future hiring needs.
What We're Looking For
5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, ideally at startups or fast-growing technology companies.
Strong experience hiring Software Engineers, AI Engineers, Product Managers, Product Designers, Visual Designers.
Experience working in small, fast-paced startup environments where priorities change quickly.
A strong sourcer who enjoys finding great passive candidates.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
Highly organized with strong attention to detail, especially with data integrity in our Ashby ATS!
Comfortable working directly with founders and senior leaders.

Experience recruiting Product Marketing or other GTM roles.
Experience recruiting for AI, SaaS, or consumer technology companies.
Experience using Ashby ATS.

About The Role
OpusClip is the world's #1 AI video agent for social media, used by 20M+ creators and businesses to turn raw footage into viral-ready clips. We're hiring an AI Product Manager , based in Mountain View , to own the core product roadmap that shapes how millions of creators experience OpusClip every day. Your job is to keep raising the bar on what our product can do and how good it feels, at the pace of a team that ships constantly.
This role sits at the AI end of that roadmap. You'll own the features where model capability is the product, which means going deeper than most PMs do on what the models can actually deliver and on how we measure whether the output is any good.
You'll work out of our headquarters, in the same market as most of our creators and business customers. The people you build for are a coffee away rather than a time zone away, and we expect you to use that.
What You'll Do
Own a Direction, Not a Backlog: Set the strategy for your surface, commit to the metrics it should move, and be the one accountable when they don't move.
Own the AI Quality Loop: Define what "good output" means for a generative feature, build the evaluation that measures it, and use that eval to decide what ships and what doesn't. On an AI product, taste alone isn't enough and a benchmark alone isn't either.
Be the Taste and Quality Bar: Act as the filter for what "good" looks like on a product used by millions. Every feature should feel considered, polished, and worth the user's trust.
Ship at Scale and Breadth: Run multiple feature workstreams in parallel without losing depth or craft. Know when to go deep on one feature and when to parallelize across several.
Codify a Repeatable Playbook: Turn your instincts into a method for how to scope, validate, and ship AI-powered features fast, and use it to raise the bar for the broader PM team, not just your own roadmap.
Partner Deeply with Engineering and Design: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with a high-caliber team to translate frontier AI capabilities (multimodal models, agents) into features creators reach for daily.
Go Deep with Users: Use direct research, data, and hands-on product use to find the gap between what the product does today and what creators actually need next.
What We're Looking For
5+ years of product management experience, with a track record of owning and shipping complex, high-usage features on a consumer or prosumer product
Deep, hands-on fluency with AI. You judge a model's real capability from your own testing rather than from its benchmark scores, and you can tell a model problem from a prompt problem from a product problem.
Comfort with evaluation. You've had to decide whether a generative output is good enough to ship when there was no obvious metric, and you built something repeatable to answer it rather than relying on vibes.
Goal-oriented and ruthless about priority. You work backward from the outcome you own, not the backlog. You can say why the top three things on your roadmap are the top three, and why everything else waits.
Ownership by default. You chase the loose ends nobody assigned to you, and you close the loop yourself: ship it, read the data, decide to iterate or kill it.
Defensible taste. You can name what is wrong with the products you admire most, not only what is good about them.
Experience building consumer-facing (B2C) products and a habit of direct user research
Based in the Bay Area and able to work on-site in Mountain View; comfortable partnering daily with our Shanghai and Vancouver teams across time zones
Bonus If You Have
Built evals for a generative feature, or worked with fine-tuned or post-trained models in production
Background taking a product from early PMF to a mature, high-scale stage
Experience with short-form video, content creation, or creator tools
Direct experience shipping AI/LLM-powered features
Ability to prototype using code or no-code tools
This Role Probably Isn't Right For You If…
You're energized by 0-to-1 ambiguity but lose interest once a product has real scale and real constraints
Your experience with AI is mostly reading about it. This role needs someone who has put their hands on the models.
You'd rather define strategy from a slide than get hands-on with the craft of a specific feature
You need a large team or established process to feel effective. This role expects you to build the playbook, not just follow one.
You haven't used a video editing or content creation tool yourself in the past year
You're uncomfortable operating with ambiguity and rapid iteration
You want remote or hybrid

We're hiring an Influencer Partnership Manager to scale our creator program. You'll find, sign, and launch creator partnerships at high volume. You'll also build real, long-term relationships with the creators who matter most to our brand.
This is a hands-on execution role. You'll run outreach and negotiations across hundreds of creators at once, keep a clean pipeline, and ship dozens of influencer posts every week. You also need a sharp read on the creator economy: who's growing, what formats work on each platform, what fair rates look like, and where the best opportunities are. In this role, you'll have the opportunity to work alongside some of the top creators in the world, who are at the forefront of shaping the future of the creator economy. This position reports directly to the Head of Creator Partnerships.
📝 Responsibilities
Scale outreach. Build and run high-volume outreach systems (sourcing, sequencing, follow-ups, and automation) to grow our creator pipeline every week.
Negotiate and close. Run negotiations with creators, managers, and agencies across many deals at once. Land fair rates, clear deliverables, and the usage rights we need, within budget.
Launch campaigns end to end. Own briefs, contracts, content review, posting schedules, and payments so every partnership ships on time.
Build lasting creator relationships. Turn one-off sponsorships into long-term partnerships. Be the person creators trust and want to work with again.
Know the landscape. Track creator economy trends, platform changes, and rate benchmarks. Use what you learn to sharpen who we partner with and how.
Measure and optimize. Report on views, CPM, signups, and ROI for every campaign. Double down on what works and cut what doesn't.
Own the pipeline. Keep our creator CRM and deal tracker accurate, current, and easy for the team to use.
Show up at events. Join and support the team at industry events, meet creators in person, and turn those conversations into partnerships.
Bring the creator voice inside. Share creator feedback and content insights with product and marketing.
📝 Qualifications
4+ years of hands-on experience in influencer marketing or creator partnerships, ideally at a tech or SaaS company.
A proven record of running high-volume creator programs: dozens of live partnerships at a time, managed across a full pipeline.
Strong negotiation skills, with direct experience contracting creators, talent managers, and agencies.
Deep knowledge of the creator economy across YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, and X, including formats, audiences, and rate benchmarks.
A bias for action. You move fast, follow up relentlessly, and ship campaigns while others are still planning.
Highly organized, with the systems to track hundreds of conversations without dropping one.
A data-driven approach to measuring campaign performance and making budget decisions.
A natural relationship builder. Creators enjoy working with you and come back for more.
Comfortable in a fast-paced startup where priorities shift quickly.
Passionate about AI and video.
📝 Bonus Points
You've run influencer marketing for a company that sells to marketers, SMBs, or agencies.
You already have a strong network of creators, talent managers, and agencies.
You've built outreach automation with tools like Clay, Instantly, or similar.
You have experience managing communications at scale, able to manage hundreds of relationships simultaneously.
You're a creator yourself, or you've worked closely on short-form video.
You've grown an affiliate or ambassador program.
This role might not be for you if
You're looking for a sales, business development, or event planning role.
You prefer strategy decks over hands-on execution.
You've mostly managed a handful of high-touch deals and haven't run outreach at scale.
You see creators purely as ad inventory rather than as long-term partners.
The details
Location: remote, preferably based in Los Angeles
Travel to industry events and creator meetups as needed
Offers equity and performance-based bonus
Medical, dental, and vision coverage
A chance to shape one of the fastest-moving categories in AI

About The Role
We are looking for a senior, full-cycle Account Executive to join our B2B team and grow OpusClip's business and enterprise customer base. You will generate pipeline, run discovery, demonstrate the product, navigate complex buying groups, negotiate commercial terms, and close new business.
This is not a role for someone who depends on an established territory, a traditional BDR team, or a fixed sales playbook. Our go-to-market motion is AI-native and supported by GTM engineering (Anthropic wrote about us here), but Account Executives are expected to create a meaningful share of their own pipeline.
What You'll Do
Own the Full Sales Cycle
Prospect into target accounts and generate a meaningful share of your own pipeline.
Run thoughtful discovery that uncovers business needs, workflows, decision criteria, and measurable value.
Deliver compelling product demonstrations tailored to users, champions, and executive buyers.
Build business cases, multi-thread across buying groups, navigate procurement and security, and lead negotiations through signature.
Close both faster-moving business and mid-market opportunities and complex enterprise deals.
Maintain a balanced pipeline rather than relying on a single large opportunity to hit your target.
Own accurate CRM hygiene, forecasting, next steps, and deal strategy.
Help Build an AI-Native Go-to-Market Motion
Partner with our GTM engineer to use AI, data, and automation to identify and engage high-potential accounts.
Test new outbound strategies, messaging, use cases, pricing, and positioning.
Adapt as we expand from media into new customer segments, including marketing teams at technology, financial services, and other enterprises.
Turn what you learn in the market into actionable feedback for Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and leadership.
Help improve the sales motion without waiting for a complete playbook.
Close the Right Customers
Qualify rigorously for customer need, urgency, product fit, and likelihood of long-term success.
Sell with integrity and avoid forcing deals that are unlikely to adopt or renew.
Partner closely with Customer Success on clean handoffs and durable account plans.
Identify expansion paths while setting realistic expectations with customers.
What We're Looking For
Required
5+ years of quota-carrying B2B SaaS sales experience, including ownership of the full sales cycle.
A demonstrated record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets.
Experience closing six-figure enterprise contracts with multiple stakeholders and long, complex sales cycles.
Ability and willingness to close smaller $20,000–$50,000 opportunities efficiently while building larger strategic deals.
Strong outbound and pipeline-generation skills; you do not wait for qualified meetings to appear on your calendar.
Excellent discovery, demonstration, negotiation, and closing ability.
Disciplined forecasting and pipeline management, with evidence that you build multiple paths to target.
Experience succeeding in a startup or another fast-changing environment with limited structure.
Adaptability: you can learn new products, buyers, industries, and sales motions quickly.
Sound judgment, resilience, and a customer-first approach to qualification.
Willingness to travel occasionally for customer meetings and industry events.
Especially Valuable
Experience selling video, content creation, social media, marketing, or other creative workflow software.
Familiarity with the needs of media companies, content teams, and enterprise marketers.
Experience using AI, automation, and data creatively in outbound prospecting and account research.
Experience selling new products or entering markets where the playbook was still being built.
Industry relationships are welcome, but they are not a substitute for sales craft. We are looking for a proven seller who can create opportunities and close business beyond an existing personal network.
What Success Looks Like
You will ramp into the product, market, and active pipeline quickly, then build repeatable pipeline of your own. You will close near-term opportunities without losing focus on enterprise accounts, forecast with accuracy, and demonstrate that you can move between different customer segments as our business evolves.
Success means consistently delivering revenue while bringing in customers who adopt OpusClip, realize value, and are positioned to renew and expand.
Why Join OpusClip
Competitive Base Salary + Equity + Uncapped Commission. On-target earnings (OTE) up to $140K–$190K annually
Sell a category-leading AI product already used by more than 10 million creators and businesses.
Work with leading media organizations and enterprise marketing teams.
Join an AI-native go-to-market team that pairs strong sellers with GTM engineering.
Help define how a fast-growing company sells new products to new markets.
Receive competitive compensation with a performance-based variable component, plus comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits.
Location
US Remote OR NYC | East Coast Preferred

We’re hiring a Lead Creative Technologist to build and run the industry’s #1 video preset library.
A preset is how AI Producer (AIP) edits: the cut rhythm, the hook, the captions, the B-roll, the music, and the motion that turn a raw upload into a video people finish watching. You own two things. Inside the product , the presets AIP ships with and the system taste prompts that decide what “good” looks like. Outside the product , our open preset library: the public collection creators install, star, and share, and our main organic growth channel.
This is a creator-operator role. You edit video at a high level, you see styles rising before they peak, and you can turn a reference into a preset others reuse. You run the library like a product: ship weekly, measure what lands, cut what doesn’t. You do it with coding agents in the loop, and you build in public as you go.
What You'll Do
Own the in-product presets and taste prompts. Define, author, and curate every preset AIP ships and the system prompts behind them. Write the taste rubric: the specific criteria for pacing, hooks, captions, B-roll, and music that separate a good edit from a passable one. Maintain golden and held-out test sets of real footage, evaluate every system prompt change against them, and show measurable progress release over release. Decide what ships and what gets cut.
Grow the open preset library. Run it as our organic growth channel: publish presets, drive stars, impressions, and installs, and make it the place creators go for editing styles.
Build in public. Prototype on the newest models and rendering techniques as they land, post what works, and turn every preset launch into reach for OpusClip and for yourself.
Edit the way top creators edit. Pacing, hooks, B-roll, captions, music, and motion. Direct agents to cut, composite, and render in the browser, then review every frame until it clears the bar.
Turn references into presets. Spot rising styles on TikTok, Reels, and YouTube, reverse-engineer what makes them work, and encode them as presets. Scale the reference library instead of hand-tuning prompts one at a time.
Ship on a cadence. Weekly preset output with a review loop. Track usage and conversion for in-product presets; stars, impressions, and installs for the open library. Double down on what performs.
Own it end-to-end. Scope the work, make the calls, ship without waiting for direction.
What We're Looking For
Video editing craft (hard requirement). Pacing, cut timing, B-roll selection, hooks and CTAs, captions, music and SFX. You’ve shipped short-form talking-head edits that performed, and you can explain why. Your portfolio shows those edits, not only motion pieces. Motion design is a plus, not a substitute.
Trend sense. You watch what’s rising across platforms, you can name the style, and you can break a reference down into the choices that make it work.
Reference-led thinking. You’d rather build a library of great references and derive from it than hand-tune prompts one at a time.
Operator instincts. You’ve run something on a cadence with numbers attached: a channel, a template library, a content program, an open-source project. You know your metrics and you move them.
Build-in-public track record. A social presence or GitHub profile where people can see what you make and how you think.
AI-native by default. You already work as a manager of agents: writing specs, having one agent review another, and authoring prompts or skills that others build on, not just one-off generations.
Comfortable in our stack. You can read and own browser code an agent helped write (HTML, GSAP, three.js), and you can open Figma or After Effects when a preset needs it. Editing craft comes first; we can teach the stack.
Sharp taste. You can tell great from merely functional, and you know when the agent got it wrong.
Judgment over tool fluency. Models will stay jagged and tools will keep changing. We care less about which stack you know and more about whether you make sound calls with little supervision.
Experience leading a small creative or technical team, formally or as the person others look to for direction and review.
Bonus: an audience of your own as a creator; 3D (Blender, Cinema 4D), shaders, creative coding, or generative/procedural effects.

Portfolio. Short-form talking-head edits first, then motion work, ideally some of it made with agents. Tell us which pieces performed and why.
Social or GitHub. Where you build in public: a channel, a profile, a repo. Anything with a history.

Run themed challenges around what the product needs next, with a prize pool split by how often each preset gets used. Creatives who also promote OpusClip through our creator partnerships team can earn on both sides.
Guard the bar. Write the rubric (pacing, hooks, captions, motion, no AI look), run every submission yourself and score it, give feedback people actually use, and decide what ships. Work with engineers and our creative technologists to get it live in the product.

Roots in the AI creative scene. You know who’s making the most exciting AI video and motion work right now, and plenty of them would answer your DM.

An AI-native operator. Agents handle your outreach, review, and reporting, so you can run a big network on your own.
